answer_1.quote: We introduce a novel framework, grounded in Nonviolent Communication Theory, for simulating and detecting communication breakdowns using relationship-contextualized LLMs. ... We contribute a dataset of 5,772 simulated conversations between familiar social partners ... In the area of AIMC, text rewriting can be used to improve interpersonal outcomes like empathy or social connection by suggesting changes to the tone or style of a message at the right time.
answer_1.outputs: simulated conflict and non-conflict dialogues, relationship backstories, turn‑level annotations of violent/non‑violent communication acts

answer_4.quote: We conducted a between‑subjects study where participants are assigned to a positive or negative backstory. ... Two independent workers completed each HIT for inter‑annotator agreement calculation, resulting in a total of 480 annotations (3,474 turns rated across 120 conversations ... We recruited 91 human annotators/participants from Mechanical Turk ... For conversation‑level measures, we assess (1) level of sympathy ... (2) understandability ... (3) positive or negative underlying intention ... (4) whether the character was overall a problematic communicator ... (5) believability of the dialogue and backstory. For turn‑level metrics, we gather (1) the extent to which a turn is problematic ... (2) fine‑grained labels of NVC or VC communication types ... (3) how the turn will make the other character feel ...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated overall conversation measures and turn‑level metrics such as problematicness, communication type, emotional impact, sympathy, intent, and believability.
